questions.knowledge_point: Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/01b742fa8f4bf42597e8653cf6b379537d95c3789743a564064a768ca343d197.png)

The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x}+k.$ What is the value of $a+k?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.$ This means that $k=1$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x}+1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,2.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x}+1 \\ 2.5 & =\frac{a}{1}+1 \\ 1.5 & =\frac{a}{1} \\ a & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+k=1+1.5=2.5.$

questions.knowledge_point: Graphing a Stretched Negative Reciprocal Function
questions.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-\frac{6}{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To plot $y=-\frac{6}{x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/d5d93e12275c683e0a56f0ec9a0c99540a7774879cd0f8fa69151ddba68a44fa.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $6$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\frac{6}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/c525edcf937bfdc311acd0d7cac778802e1939dc2bd61fd3a5bf58f808712220.png)

questions.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{4}{5x}+3?$
